hot.title: H-JEPA: End-to-End Learning of Hierarchical World Models for Visual Planning
hot.summary: H-JEPA plans visual tasks by learning three predictive levels, with each higher level predicting farther ahead in its own latent space and passing subgoals to finer planners. In a 50-task simulated AntMaze evaluation, three-level H-JEPA reaches 73.3% success, versus 18.0% for flat LeWM. A separate compute sweep shows a higher-success, lower-planner-compute frontier, not a wall-clock speedup; evidence is from simulation and offline DROID evaluation.

hot.title: Truly Subquadratic 3SUM and Truly Subcubic APSP via Triangles in Sparse Lopsided Graphs
hot.summary: The authors introduce a deterministic algorithm that computes selected entries of a thin matrix product without computing the full product or each entry separately. It recursively multiplies rectangular matrices and prunes work for unrequested outputs. It gives 3SUM in O(n^1.9992) and directed APSP in O(n^2.9995) for polynomially bounded integers in the word-RAM model, asymptotic bounds rather than measured speedups.

hot.title: Base Models Can Reason By Taking a Cue From Training Data
hot.summary: The authors test whether short fixed openings can elicit reasoning from language models without changing their weights. On MATH-500, Olmo-3-7B pass@1 rises from 42% without a cue to 78% with “Okay,” versus 75% after reinforcement learning. In a controlled data-edit experiment, renaming “okay” to “chicken” makes “Chicken” effective, supporting cue effects in these tested settings, not all models.

hot.title: LiFT: Loop Flow Transformers
hot.summary: LiFT uses a shared transformer core within each diffusion step, training passes to refine velocity estimates along a correction path. On class-conditional ImageNet-1k at 256×256, LiFT-L/2 R10 run with eight loops and 50 steps reaches FID 10.95 at 28.24 TFLOPs per image, versus dense DiT-XL/2 with 250 steps at FID 14.30. This unguided, cross-scale comparison does not establish latency savings or generalization.

hot.title: Mulligan: Performance-Guided Data Collection for Efficient On-Robot Learning
hot.summary: Mulligan guides robot-learning data collection by choosing some starting states where the policy failed while using coverage-based choices to explore less-tried states. Operators correct and replay tasks, while a critic learns from all rollouts. On Insert Marker, full HiL-IDQL+Mulligan achieved 76% success versus 42% for uniform HG-DAgger; evidence is limited to studied tasks and operator-placeable starts.

hot.title: Optimal and Efficient Online Inverse Optimization
hot.summary: The paper presents online inverse linear optimization with revocable directional updates, learning from expert choices without observing the hidden objective or utility values. The deterministic, proper RVM learner removes a stretch after its query leaves a slab and achieves regret at most 51√d/4 for every horizon; a matching-order lower bound applies when T≥d.

hot.title: A Call for an Open Tokenizer Benchmark
hot.summary: Cognetta proposes a public benchmark for comparing text tokenizers by training language models under shared rules and scoring prediction loss in bits per byte of original text. The design fixes most model and training choices while allowing tokenizer-dependent vocabulary sizes. Bits-per-byte scores each tokenizer’s canonical segmentation. The paper reports no benchmark results or validated predictive metrics, and leaves batching unresolved.

hot.title: LoGRA: Scaling LLM Reinforcement Learning with Low-Rank Gradient Sketches
hot.summary: LoGRA lowers training memory in LLM reinforcement-learning post-training by accumulating compact gradient sketches, applying approximate updates to full weights, and reusing factors for rollout synchronization. Its predicted-KL controller scales updates to limit next-token probability changes. For Qwen2.5-Math-7B, average memory was 17.29 GiB versus 31.82 GiB with dense Adam, with peak Pass@1 of 72.33% versus 72.48% across three seeds. At 27B, dense Adam ran out of memory, leaving no matched comparison.

hot.title: UndoBench: Separating Task Competence from Recovery Capability in Tool-Using AI Agents
hot.summary: The authors introduce UndoBench to evaluate whether AI agents recover safely when external operations fail. It pairs identical-seed control and faulted runs, measuring recovery only when the control succeeds, and records external effects. Across 12 held-out workflows, control success was 83.54%, but conditional recovery was 46.72%; results cover sandboxed trials with one lost acknowledgment fault.

hot.title: OpenWAM: An Open Framework for Composable World-Action Models
hot.summary: OpenWAM tests links between video predictions and robot actions, including reuse of action models. It compares generation routes in a shared framework and trains separate dynamics models on demonstrations and counterfactual transitions. After target-task video adaptation, a frozen local-context inverse dynamics model achieves 84.0% mean closed-loop success across four held-out LIBERO-90 simulation targets, versus 47.0% for full-context conditioning.

hot.title: Priced Guidance: Can Language Models Generate Future Research Ideas?
hot.summary: Priced Guidance measures information needed for a model to recover an existing research idea. A generator assigns probabilities to answers; a target-informed guide selects among them, and less likely answers cost more bits. Expected cost bounds unguided acceptance from below. The ensemble’s median Essence cost was 55.8 bits, versus 69.9 for Fable 5.1 alone, measuring guided recovery rather than independent research generation.

hot.title: QF3: Fast Flow RL with Filtered Q-Gradients
hot.summary: QF3 addresses robot learning by improving flow policies from replayed experience. It anchors policy updates to replay actions through flow matching, then applies a critic gradient to a one-step action prediction, clipping velocity corrections that stray too far from the replay target. In tested settings, clipping prevents collapse; on G1 dance tracking, training reaches full episodes about 10 times faster than FPO++.

hot.title: Video Encoders Built on Image Representations
hot.summary: The method represents sampled video frames independently, then uses a question-aware selector to choose a fixed set of relevant, diverse candidates before a lightweight refiner adds neighboring-frame context. On Qwen3-VL-8B, it scores 62.75 on the unweighted 13-benchmark average with 1,535 visual tokens, versus 62.58 for full Image input with 4,424 tokens. This supports similar aggregate accuracy, not uniform benchmark gains.

hot.title: Level-of-Token Diffusion
hot.summary: LoT allocates image and video transformer tokens according to desired detail, using larger patches in simple regions and smaller patches where detail matters. A transformer processes the shorter sequence, while extent-aware flow recovery produces a full-resolution denoising field. At matched 2× video token budget, LoT reports 2.262× speedup and higher Aesthetic and Imaging scores than Foveated Diffusion, but not higher Dynamic Degree at the highest tested compression.

hot.title: ThunderSyncRL: Lossless Acceleration of Agentic Reinforcement Learning
hot.summary: ThunderSyncRL streams learner gradient calculations as trajectory rewards or teacher scores become available, while keeping rollouts and gradients tied to one policy snapshot and applying one optimizer step after the batch completes. In the reported Qwen-3.8-27B GRPO setup, it reaches 74.01% pass@3 on SWE-bench Verified in 121.3 GPU-hours versus 233.5 with Sync, a 1.9× speedup; outcomes depend on workload overlap.

hot.title: VeriFine: Scaling Verification for Self-Improvement in Embodied Reasoning
hot.summary: VeriFine adapts a policy, its curriculum, and its judge as failures change. Its reference-free rubric judge evaluates reasoning against context, while policy and judge loops select examples and have humans refine unreliable judgments. Across three driving rounds, reasoning scores rise from 60.56 to 71.61, an 18.2% relative gain; evidence covers driving and robot navigation, not every task.

hot.title: SheetSage2: Coherent Lead-Sheet Transcription with Synthetic Supervision
hot.summary: SheetSage2 converts audio into lead sheets by predicting musical attributes from MIDI-rendered training audio, decoding them on a shared musical grid, and distilling complete event sequences into one autoregressive model. Its structured decoder improves melody octave consistency: octave mixing falls from 12.91% to 9.31% on 333 R-W-C passages. This measures within-passage consistency, not whether the selected octave is correct.

hot.title: Introducing Beam: Reflection’s 501B open-weight model
hot.summary: Reflection introduces Beam, its first open-weight model: a sparse Mixture-of-Experts with 501 billion total and 23 billion active parameters, aimed at coding, reasoning, and agentic workloads. It was pretrained on 23.8 trillion curated tokens and then trained with a high-compute reinforcement learning run of over 100 million rollouts on 10.5K NVIDIA GB300 GPUs. Beam is competitive with larger open models while using far less inference compute, and its weights are slated for release under Apache 2.0 later in the month.

hot.title: I-BFM: Reward-Conditioned Robust Humanoid Interaction via Unsupervised Reinforcement Learning
hot.summary: I-BFM addresses humanoid-object interaction by learning a shared policy that represents robot, object, and contact state and is directed by task rewards. It acts closed-loop rather than following a fixed trajectory. In simulated MuJoCo Carry Box, it achieves 94.3% nominal success and 89.3% after a specified robot fall, versus OmniContact’s 1.3%; these rates are task-completion results under that perturbation.

hot.title: InterMimicGen: Scaling Humanoid Loco-Manipulation through Self-Evolving Motion Imitation
hot.summary: InterMimicGen expands humanoid motion references by editing object paths or body postures, training a physics-based tracker on edits, and retaining motions that execute in simulation. In a bimanual G1 setting with Inspire hands, references grow 21.8× after round one and 150.5× after round five, while tracker success on accepted references rises from 52.1% to 98.4%. This densifies existing interactions rather than creating new tasks.

likes.title: Towards Looped Models Done Right Part II: Rethinking at Fixed Points
likes.summary: The paper trains a looped language model to settle toward fixed points across repeated applications of a shared block. Terminal key-value (KV) sharing retains only final cache banks; separate methods reuse endpoints for prefill and reinforcement learning. At 1.6B parameters, the learned-depth-prior model scores 60.00% on the downstream average with four rather than twelve KV banks, in the reported setup.

likes.title: Finetuning with Sampling: SFT Learns Better Than You Think
likes.summary: Projection sampling transforms expert demonstrations into responses more like those of a pretrained model before standard supervised fine-tuning, using the model to propose continuations and an MCMC procedure to select them. On Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, it raises SciKnowEval Chemistry L-3 single-shot accuracy to 66.0%, while the five-task prior-capability average is 58.6%, below the base model’s 59.7%.

likes.title: Looped Diffusion Transformer
likes.summary: Looped-DiT improves text-to-image generation by repeating shared middle Transformer blocks within each denoising step, refining hidden representations without adding unique parameters. Deep Supervision trains intermediate predictions, and Self-Modulating Attention regulates repeated updates. Its B/16 model averages 71.5 across six benchmarks versus 69.0 for 1.7B InternVL-U, at 150 versus 732 TFLOPs per image, in 260M-parameter pixel-space models using 512 × 512 resolution.

likes.title: ScholarCatalyst: A Benchmark for Retrieving Papers That Inspire New Research
likes.summary: ScholarCatalyst benchmarks whether systems can retrieve prior papers that project authors judged helpful or potentially helpful to early-stage research. It uses 894 retrospectively annotated queries from 207 computer-science projects, with author-labeled positives and hard negatives. Across its reported settings, agentic search reaches overall Recall@20 of 0.42 versus 0.48 for embedding retrieval, measuring retrospective judgments rather than successful inspiration.

likes.title: Decoding Looped Transformers Better for (Almost) Free
likes.summary: LoopCD guides looped Transformers by extrapolating from an earlier prediction toward the final prediction for the same prefix, without adding recurrent iterations. It offers logits and hidden-state variants, with hidden-state guidance avoiding an extra output pass. On AIME 2024, adaptive LoopCD-Logits raises Ouro-2.6B-Thinking pass@1 from 61.88% to 73.33%; results are not uniformly positive across tasks and metrics.

likes.title: VISTA: A Visual Harness for Reasoning in an Interactive World
likes.summary: VISTA gives a multimodal model access to archived game frames, allowing it to retrieve earlier images, compare moments, and enlarge details while reasoning in language and choosing actions. Across 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games, Claude Opus 5.0 completes all games with a mean Relative Human Action Efficiency score of 100.00, using 7,302 actions versus 17,135 for first-time humans. This public-set result does not establish performance on unseen games.

likes.title: SkillRefiner: Offline Skill Refinement from Historical Agent Traces
likes.summary: SKILLREFINER refines an agent’s reusable instructions from traces and feedback without generating new executions during refinement. It summarizes and clusters runs by outcome, proposes edits, and checks failure-derived edits against evidence before merging. On 200 held-out SpreadsheetBench tasks, it reached 84.0% accuracy versus 79.0% for Trace2Skill and 78.5% for GEPA; token comparisons exclude collection costs and do not establish computation.

likes.title: Sharpening Tax in Post-Training
likes.summary: The authors compare base and post-trained agents on three agentic benchmarks across repeated rollouts, and introduce Sharpening Tax to measure how much success retries recover. For Gemma-4-31B on WebShop, the harness-equipped base model rises from 22.7% pass@1 to 87.6% pass@128, while its post-trained counterpart reaches 39.5% and 56.0%. The comparison is observational and varies by model scale and rollout budget.

likes.title: Kolibri: A Sovereign European Model on the Pareto Frontier
likes.summary: Kolibri is an open-weight bilingual model designed for local deployment on controlled infrastructure. It activates 3.46B of 78.1B parameters per token and uses sliding-window attention in 40 of 50 blocks, with full attention in every fifth block. Against Kolibri Origin, its post-trained scores are higher in English and German, with 2.7× reported decode throughput under the paper’s measurement setup.

likes.title: Sphere Encoder 2
likes.summary: Sphere Encoder 2 trains a decoder to reconstruct near encoded points and generate from random points near the sphere’s equator, replacing limited noise and pixel reconstruction loss with rotation-based training and feature-space score matching. On ImageNet at 256×256, Sphere2-L† reports FDr6 4.92 at 4×2 NFE, versus PixNerd-XL’s 5.01 at 100×2 NFE; this compares sampling compute, not wall-clock time.

likes.title: Learning Functional Subspaces for Neural Network Compression
likes.summary: LSP compresses neural networks by learning which directions to remove from linear layers rather than local spectra. It trains projectors against output distributions while freezing weights, after allocating ranks using output-KL costs. On Llama-2-7B at 70% compression, LSP reaches 10.9 WikiText-2 perplexity versus 13.3 for SVD-LLM and 222.8 for untrained NoLSP, under reported calibration protocols.

likes.title: Scaling and Distilling Text Embeddings for Better Diffusibility
likes.summary: This paper improves continuous diffusion language models by distilling a smaller encoder to preserve a teacher’s probabilities over plausible next words, bringing their embeddings closer. On OWT-1024, ELF-M reaches generated-text perplexity 17.8±0.1 at entropy 5.45±0.01, versus 19.3±0.2 for raw T5Gemma-2, using 512 rather than 256 denoiser evaluations. This quality comparison is not at equal compute.

likes.title: JEPA-TTT: Persistent Test-Time Training of Latent World Models for Planning under Dynamics Shifts
likes.summary: JEPA-TTT adapts a world model’s latent dynamics predictor during deployment, using observed transitions while keeping its visual encoder and offline-trained reward head fixed. A planner uses the updated predictor to choose actions without goal images or online rewards. Across eight shifts in four environments, it improves planning scores over frozen JEPA on every shift; the study tests only a single persistent dynamics change.

likes.title: PivotOPD: Learning to Recover from Pivotal Mistakes in Multi-Turn Agents
likes.summary: PivotOPD trains multi-turn agents to avoid pivotal mistakes and recover from the states those mistakes create. A teacher supplies gold actions for prevention and recovery responses for later turns, combining these signals with group-based reinforcement learning. On ALFWorld, Qwen3-1.7B reaches 73.7% success versus 68.2% for SDAR; recovery evidence is principally oracle-labeled ALFWorld analysis.

likes.title: Reconstruct, Practice, Go Real: Guided Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents
likes.summary: RPG lets robot skills improve through practice without changing model weights. It revises reusable executable skills and system prompts using failure diagnosis, then validates candidate and merged changes across tasks. In simulation, held-out success across 22 manipulation tasks rose from 63/220 (28.6%) after round 1 to 209/220 (95.0%) after round 15; this is not matched-compute evidence.

likes.title: Scaling Laws for Looped Mixture of Experts
likes.summary: The paper develops a sparsity-conditional scaling law for looped Mixture-of-Experts models, estimating recurrence’s bounded capacity benefit while accounting for active and total parameters. Fitted to held-out loss, it predicts expert-count slices better than a sparsity-independent bounded model, with RMSE 0.0047 versus 0.0075. At 5×10²⁰ training FLOPs, 0.3B-active models with E≥8 outperform 1.0B dense models on reported aggregates.

likes.title: Ego2Act: Evaluating Goal-Directed Manipulation in Egocentric Video Generation
likes.summary: Ego2Act evaluates whether video generators turn an egocentric starting scene and outcome-oriented goal into valid rollouts. It scores task completion and physical plausibility separately, combining normalized scores with a geometric mean. On a 25-case panel, Seedance-2.0 scores 64.0 Final; Ego2ActJudge correlates with human consensus at Pearson r = 0.69. These results do not establish downstream planning or learning benefits.
